Explain how transformers work in machine learning at a high level.

Transformers are a neural network architecture introduced in the paper "Attention is All You Need" (2017). The key innovation is the self-attention mechanism, which allows the model to weigh the importance of different words in a sequence relative to each other.

At a high level: input tokens are converted to embeddings, positional encoding is added, then multiple layers of multi-head self-attention and feed-forward networks process the sequence. This allows the model to capture long-range dependencies much better than RNNs.

What is multi-head attention specifically?

Multi-head attention runs multiple attention operations ("heads") in parallel, each learning different aspects of relationships between tokens. The outputs are then concatenated and projected.

Each head computes: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V where Q, K, V are learned linear projections of the input.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // num_heads
        self.W_q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
